summary_html: Family agrees to a **voluntary service plan**—counseling, substance-use treatment, parenting classes—designed to correct conditions without court compulsion. Federal law prioritizes family preservation through prevention and support services.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Mary Ellen C. v. Arizona Department of Economic Security
key_cases.holding: The court of appeals reversed the severance order because the State failed to make reasonable efforts to preserve the family, holding that the duty to provide rehabilitative services with a reasonable possibility of success has a constitutional basis.
key_cases.relevance: The foundational Arizona statement of what an adequate service plan must look like.
key_cases.quote: although the State is not obliged to undertake futile rehabilitative measures, it is obliged to undertake those which offer a reasonable possibility of success

key_cases.case_name: Mary Lou C. v. Arizona Department of Economic Security
key_cases.holding: The court of appeals affirmed the severance order, holding that the State's constitutionally grounded obligation to make a reasonable effort to preserve the family applies to the prior-severance ground of A.R.S. § 8-533(B)(10) as it does to other grounds, but affirming because the record supported an implicit finding that further rehabilitative services would have been futile.
key_cases.relevance: The leading post-Mary Ellen C. Arizona application of the rule that offered services must be genuine, holding the preservation duty is constitutionally rooted rather than merely statutory.
key_cases.quote: The requirement that ADES make an effort to preserve the family is mandated on constitutional grounds

key_cases.case_name: Shawanee S. v. Arizona Department of Economic Security
key_cases.holding: The court of appeals affirmed the termination order, holding that although the agency must prove a diligent effort to provide appropriate reunification services on a length-of-time-in-care ground, a parent who never objects in the juvenile court waives an appellate challenge to that finding.
key_cases.relevance: Shows that a parent must contest the adequacy of offered services contemporaneously, not later.
key_cases.quote: when ADES seeks severance based on length of time in care, ADES must prove that it "has made a diligent effort to provide appropriate reunification services."

key_cases.case_name: Jessie D. v. Department of Child Safety
key_cases.holding: The Arizona Supreme Court affirmed termination of an incarcerated father's rights, holding that although the juvenile court misapplied a Michael J. factor, DCS owes incarcerated parents a diligent effort to preserve the family and reasonable evidence supported the best-interests finding.
key_cases.relevance: States the agency's affirmative service obligation that underlies any voluntary service plan offered short of court compulsion.
key_cases.quote: DCS must make diligent efforts to preserve the family by providing services to assist parents in maintaining a bond with their children

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives
